child: Write a little note to {member} telling them one thing you like about them.
adult: Write a short letter to {member} about something you appreciate in them but haven't said.

child: Is something hard to say out loud? Write it in a note to {member} instead.
adult: Is there something that feels too big to say face to face? Write it to {member} – you choose whether to share it.

child: Write a 'thank you' card to {extended}.
adult: Write a letter or voice note to {extended} telling them what they mean to you.

child: Finish this sentence in a note to {member}: 'I feel happy when you…'
adult: Finish these in a note to {member}: 'I feel close to you when…' and 'I sometimes find it hard when…'

child: Make a 'feelings flag' with {member}: green = I'm OK, orange = I need a bit of space, red = I need help.
adult: Agree on a simple signal with {member} for 'I need space' or 'I need you' – a word, emoji or object on the fridge.

child: Hide a kind note somewhere {member} will find it.
adult: Leave a surprise note for {member} in their bag, lunchbox or on the mirror.

child: Start a shared notebook with {member}. Write one line and pass it on.
adult: Start a shared journal with {member}: each of you writes a few lines and passes it back and forth this week.

child: Write down a worry, then show it to someone you trust.
adult: Write about something that has been weighing on you. Then decide who, if anyone, you'd like to share it with.

child: Write a letter to future-you in a year. Seal it with {member}.
adult: Write a letter to {member} to be opened in one year. Seal it together.

child: Send {member} a message using only emojis. Can they guess what you mean?
adult: Text {member} a song that says something you'd struggle to put into words.

child: Write {member} a note about a favourite memory you share.
adult: Write {member} a short note about a memory with them that you treasure.

child: Draw a picture for {member} that shows how you feel about them today.
adult: If words won't come, send {member} a photo or picture that says how you feel about them.

child: Write {member} a note that starts with: 'Something I wish you knew about me is…'
adult: Write {member} a note that starts: 'Something I wish you knew about me is…' Share it only if you want to.

child: Write {member} a 'thank you for' list – at least 3 things!
adult: Write {member} a list of small, everyday things they do that you're grateful for.

child: Write a note to {member} about something you're worried about. Ask them to just listen.
adult: Write {member} about something you'd like help with, and how you'd like them to respond – just listen, or help fix it.

child: Choose a 'feelings colour' each night this week and tell {member}. Red, blue, yellow…?
adult: Each evening this week, share one word for your day with {member}. No need to explain.

child: Write {extended} a letter asking them about their life when they were little.
adult: Write {extended} a letter with three questions about their life you've always wondered about.

child: Make a 'question jar' with {member}. Each of you writes 3 questions to ask each other.
adult: Make a question jar with {member}: each of you adds questions, and you take one out at dinner.

child: Write {member} a note about something they did that made you proud.
adult: Write {member} about a moment you were proud of them – be specific about what they did.

child: Make a comic strip about a funny thing that happened with {member}.
adult: Write down a story about your family that you'd want your grandchildren to hear.

child: Write a letter to someone you miss. You can keep it or share it.
adult: Write a letter to someone you miss or have lost touch with. You decide what to do with it.

child: Text or voice-note {member} a 'good morning' message every day this week.
adult: Send {member} a short message each day this week – a thought, a song or a 'thinking of you'.
